correctness.rationale: The one-step P(t) is row stochastic with nonzero weights at least eta; each two-step action row has every entry >=eta^2. If the limiting full diameter remained positive, actions are uniformly interior, so maximal and minimal persistent opinions must eventually be constant isolated leaders. Their excluded cross-action distances sum to (1+phi)D_infty, strictly exceeding 2 epsilon, contradicting 2 epsilon >=(1+phi)D0. After diameter falls below epsilon the complete-neighborhood P_* has P_*^2 positive, giving geometric convergence. A stationary two-agent witness for every smaller radius proves sharpness. The bundled exact-rational verifier reconstructs finite matrix identities, not the infinity proof.
